spec:
Vocabulary ids: 0 <pad>, 1 <bos>, 2 <eos>, 3 ' ', 4 ',', 5 '.', 6 '!', 7 '?', 8 "'", 9 '"', 10..35 = a..z (a=10, e=14, i=18, o=24, u=30, y=34). Input ctx [8,36]: one-hot rows, oldest first, row 7 = most recent token; an all-zero row means 'before document start'. LETTER row = token in 10..35. BOUNDARY row = an all-zero row, or a row whose token is not a letter and is not the apostrophe (id 8) [so bos, space, , . ! ? and the double quote are boundaries; the apostrophe is NOT]. 'word so far' = the maximal run of LETTER rows ending at row 7 (or at the row named in the rule); it is 'anchored' when the row just before the run exists and is a BOUNDARY row. Evidence output y [36] is added to next-token logits by the parent, in nats; 0 means 'no opinion'. Entries for ids 0,1 must be exactly 0 unless a rule says otherwise; id 2 (<eos>) is 0 unless a rule says otherwise. Case 'note' fields explain the case; 'expect' vectors are index 0..35 in vocabulary order and must be matched within tol. Inputs are exact one-hot / 0-1 values. Tables in 'data' are authoritative and must not be changed. You may write a helper script that expands 'data' into proposal JSON. Each cell/param holds at most 40 numbers (spread lookups over many cells and combine with ops; ops on ctx rows such as slice/mul/sum are exact and free of parameters).

Name-cache writer (state update). Inputs ctx [8,36] and nm [224] (previous cache state); output y [224] = new cache state. Layout of nm: elements 0..215 = buffer B as 6 rows x 36 (row-major:
element 36*i+t is 1 iff the i-th captured letter has token id t); element 216 = cap (1 while a name is being captured, else 0); elements 217..223 = one-hot of L (the number of letters captured, 0..6).
Rules, in priority order, evaluated on this step's ctx (row 7 = the token just emitted):
 1. TRIGGER: if rows 2..7 of ctx are exactly n,a,m,e,d,space (ids 23,10,22,14,13,3): output buffer all zeros, cap = 1, L = 0 (element 217 = 1, the rest of 217..223 = 0).
 2. elif cap >= 0.5 and row 7 is a letter: if L < 6: set B[L] to the one-hot of row 7 and advance L by one (one-hot shifts to L+1); if L == 6: nothing changes; cap stays 1.
 3. elif cap >= 0.5 (row 7 is not a letter): cap = 0, buffer and L unchanged.
 4. else: output = input unchanged.
The state inputs are always valid (0/1 values, L one-hot, buffer rows one-hot for i < L, zero rows beyond). Meaning: remembers the letters of the most recent 'named <word>' (protagonist names like 'lily'), up to 6 letters.
